item.title: Report – Milan Owner Gerry Cardinale Makes Real Madrid Starlet His Priority Ahead of Tresoldi
item.description: Report – Milan Owner Gerry Cardinale Makes Real Madrid Starlet His Priority Ahead of Tresoldi Milan appear to have settled on Endrick as their preferred attacking target for January, with Gerry Cardinale reportedly favouring the Real Madrid youngster over Nicolo Tresoldi. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Rossoneri owner has personally accelerated the pursuit of the Brazilian after publicly expressing his admiration for the 20-year-old. Cardinale left little doubt about his intentions when discussing the transfer market, describing Endrick as one of the most gifted youngsters in the world in his position, if not the most talented. The Brazilian has struggled for regular playing time at the Santiago Bernabeu, accumulating just 160 minutes between La Liga and the Champions League this season. However, Jose Mourinho remains reluctant to sanction Endrick’s departure, considering he has been an important part of his plans at Real Madrid. Endrick is also reportedly happy in the Spanish capital, meaning Milan could face considerable obstacles in their pursuit. Milan Chief Prefers Endrick to Tresoldi Although Nicolo Tresoldi remains on Milan’s shortlist, Cardinale considers Endrick a more attractive option because of his versatility. The Real Madrid forward can operate as a center-forward, a right-sided attacker or an attacking midfielder, making him a potentially valuable addition to Ruben Amorim’s tactical system. By contrast, Tresoldi offers a more traditional center-forward profile, potentially complicating his integration alongside Goncalo Ramos. The Club Brugge youngster has also attracted Bayern Munich’s attention, particularly following Harry Kane’s injury. Milan could nevertheless benefit from Cardinale’s strong relationship with Roc Nation, the agency representing Endrick. A loan move or a permanent transfer with a buy-back clause could emerge as possible solutions, although much will depend on Real Madrid’s willingness to negotiate.

item.description: Landry Shamet's contract proving to be massive bargain for Knicks originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Knicks have been guided by their stars this season, with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns picking up right where they left off, but one role player from last season's championship team has delivered on a nightly basis. Landry Shamet scored 20 points in the Knicks' last-second win over the Trail Blazers on Saturday night, producing his second 20-point game in the last four contests. In hindsight, the contract Shamet signed to return to the Knicks is looking like a bargain for New York — and it's no coincidence New York has started to look like the team it was last season with him rolling. Here's a closer look at Shamet's efforts this season. Landry Shamet proving to be Knicks bargain Shamet is making under $5.5 million this season and playing like a Sixth Man of the Year candidate, Saturday's start notwithstanding. The Knicks veteran is averaging 11.0 points per game, a career-high, and shooting 45.3 percent from 3-point range. Shamet is also shooting just under 50 percent from the field. Shamet has been essential to the Knicks' current four-game win streak, averaging 16.3 points per game and shooting 14-of-24 (58.3 percent) from 3-point range during the stretch. For Detroit, the Lions will be without center Cade Mays, who was placed on injured reserve Saturday with an ankle injury. The Lions also entered the weekend with several injury concerns in their secondary, including cornerbacks D.J. Reed, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and Khalil Dorsey, who were all listed as questionable. item.title: Dallas Cowboys fan from New Mexico dies after 49ers game altercation
item.description: Arlington police are looking into the death of a lifelong Dallas Cowboys fan days following an alleged altercation around kickoff during the game against the San Francisco 49ers, USA Today reported. The family of Mario Narro contacted police on Tuesday, Nov. 17, about the incident. Narro died on Wednesday, Nov. 18. Narro, 36, had traveled from Albuquerque to attend the NFC rivalry game when an alleged alteration with a 49ers fan ended when Narro was pushed and fell down a flight of stairs, his family told CBS News Texas and the California Post , a branch of the New York Post. His family said he had a swollen abdomen and bruising and sat through the game, but wasn't feeling well. He was taken to a stadium medical team, who then transported him to a hospital. He had multiple surgeries and died on Wednesday, Nov. 18. An official cause of death is pending. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones spoke about the fan's death on Dallas radio station 105.3 The Fan on Friday, Nov. 20. Jones said there was no record of the incident but the organization was looking into it. Jones added that the Cowboys would cooperate with authorities for any surveillance footage or information the team could find. "Let me make the point of, we really do have quite eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago, we have quite a surveillance of what's going on in every aspect of our game," Jones said. "So it is really rare if we didn't know of any incident. We've got too many people out there. We have 6,000 workers on game day." item.title: Dwight Howard Regrets Rejecting Stephen Curry Trade In 2011 And Passing On Warriors In 2013
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-USA TODAY Sports Dwight Howard regrets missing two opportunities to play alongside Stephen Curry , revealing that he opposed the Orlando Magic’s interest in acquiring the guard in 2011 before choosing the Houston Rockets over the Golden State Warriors in 2013. Speaking with Casey Kiernan on The AM Hoops Show , Howard admitted that he failed to recognize what Curry would become. At the time, he preferred Curry’s more established backcourt partner, Monta Ellis . “But I had an opportunity to play with Steph too, and I’m tripping. At the time, I wanted to play with Monta Ellis.” “The Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph, and I said no. I said no because I didn’t know Wardell Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest shooters in the world. At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes. I regret it…” Howard’s recollection describes a potential acquisition discussed with Orlando’s front office. It does not establish that the Warriors had agreed to a completed trade or that Howard formally possessed veto authority. Nevertheless, he clearly believes his preference helped close off an intriguing possibility. The numbers explain why Ellis appealed to him. In 2010-11, Ellis averaged 24.1 points and 5.6 assists while playing 40.3 minutes per game. Curry averaged 18.6 points and 5.8 assists in 33.6 minutes, although his 44.2% three-point shooting already demonstrated exceptional potential. Ellis was the more prominent scorer; Curry was still developing into the player who would transform basketball. Howard eventually left Orlando for the Los Angeles Lakers in 2012. Following one season there, he considered Golden State during his 2013 free agency before deciding to join Houston. Looking back, the possibility of sharing the floor with Curry and Klay Thompson leaves him astonished. “Me and Steph Curry? And Klay Thompson? Oh my God, what was I thinking? No, but I think that would have been a crazy team. The pick and roll with me and Steph, the pick and roll, oh my God.” The Warriors’ pursuit was real, but bringing Howard aboard required financial maneuvering. Contemporary reporting described efforts to clear salary and potential sign-and-trade arrangements involving the Lakers. Keeping every important young player while adding Howard was not necessarily guaranteed. The Warriors ultimately acquired Andre Iguodala that summer. On the court, Howard’s excitement is understandable. His screening, lob finishing, rebounding, and rim protection could have complemented Curry’s shooting beautifully. Defenses would have faced a difficult choice between stepping toward Curry and allowing Howard space to finish above the rim. item.title: ‘You criticise him too much’ – Pedri defends ‘exceptional’ Barcelona teammate after Villarreal
item.description: ‘You criticise him too much’ – Pedri defends ‘exceptional’ Barcelona teammate after Villarreal Barcelona star Pedri has on Sunday evening launched a stern defence of teammate and midfield partner Frenkie de Jong. This comes fresh off the Dutchman’s latest fine performance in Blaugrana colours. Barcelona kicked their campaign back into gear following the international break a short time ago, welcoming Villarreal to the Camp Nou for a La Liga clash. When all was said and done, the Catalans recovered from two goals down, to emerge on the right side of a 3-2 result. The aforementioned Frenkie de Jong was asked to fill an unfamiliar role for the afternoon, slotting into the heart of Barca’s backline. The former Ajax man, though, showcased his versatility and class over the course of the 90 minutes, playing a key role in his side’s eventual comeback. Speaking to the media following the full-time whistle, Pedri therefore made use of the opportunity to heap some well-earned praise on his long-time teammate: ”He’s an exceptional player, one of the best. He can play at full-back, centre-back or in midfield. With his qualities, he could probably even play in goal! He gives us so much, and I honestly think people criticise him too much. If you really watch what he does on the pitch, you’ll realise just how good he is.” Conor Laird – GSFN

Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect BYU opened as an early 12.5-point favorite over Cincinnati for Saturday’s regular-season finale in Provo, according to FanDuel . The point total is 56.5 as of this publishing. The Cougs are coming off a game that was a lot more stressful than it needed to be. BYU beat Kansas 31-29 in triple overtime. It wasn’t pretty, but it moved BYU to 9-2 overall and 6-2 in the Big 12, and it kept the Cougs’ CFP and Big 12 title game hopes in play. Cincinnati comes to Provo at 6-5 and bowl eligible after beating Colorado 35-28 Saturday. The Bearcats are top 10 nationally in rushing offense behind 1,000-yard back Cole Tabb. The defense is one of the nation’s worst, however, allowing over 30 points per game. BYU needs a “get right” game on offense, and the Bearcats offer that. We’ll get more clarity on where BYU stands in the CFP race after Tuesday’s rankings, but the Big 12 title game is still on the table too. Utah has officially clinched its spot in Arlington, so BYU and Texas Tech are competing for the second spot. As long as the Red Raiders beat TCU, they’re into the Big 12 title game. BYU would get in with a win if Texas Tech loses to TCU, because the Cougars would hold the tiebreaker of record against common opponents. Tech and TCU play Thursday in a Thanksgiving game, so BYU will know exactly what’s at stake before kickoff Saturday. The title game is Friday, December 4, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. BYU-Cincinnati play Saturday at 1:30 MT on FOX.

item.title: Chris Berman announces Tom Jackson’s death in emotional tribute on ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’
item.description: Chris Berman grew emotional Sunday while discussing Tom Jackson, his longtime ESPN broadcast partner, who died Friday at 75 . “He was a vital 75,” Berman said on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” show. “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.” Berman, who said he spoke “at length” to Jackson as recently as Tuesday, also called the former Broncos linebacker “one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.” He quoted The Temptations hit song “My Girl,” saying Jackson always “brought sunshine on a cloudy day.” Chris Berman remembers his longtime broadcast partner and dear friend, Tom Jackson, following his passing. pic.twitter.com/4pufldOXSV — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 22, 2026 ESPN commentators Tom Jackson and Chris Berman cover the game between the Chicago Bears and St. Louis Rams in St. Louis, Missouri, Dec. 11, 2006. Getty Images “All of us are stunned,” Berman read from a statement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro added that Jackson — a three-time Pro Bowler over 14 NFL seasons with the Broncos — was “one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history.” “He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans,” Pitaro said. “Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact. Sports anchors Chris Berman, left, and Tom Jackson speak during a ceremony honoring Berman with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in Hollywood, Calif. Getty Images “Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.” Jackson retired from ESPN in 2016 but returned for a digital edition of “NFL Primetime” alongside Berman in 2019. He had been awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2015, an honor which Berman also had earned in 2010. Jackson is survived by his wife, Jennifer, and two daughters, Taylor and Morgan.

item.title: ‘Where is…?’ – Knicks fans shocked by who was missing from Homecoming event at Trail Blazers game
item.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images The New York Knicks celebrated their annual Homecoming Game on Saturday night, welcoming more than 50 former players back to Madison Square Garden. However, one notable name was missing from the celebrations, as Charles Oakley was nowhere to be seen. The Knicks held a private dinner on Friday before recognising their former stars at half-time of their clash with the Portland Trail Blazers. Walt ‘Clyde’ Frazier, Bernard King and Earl Monroe were among those in attendance, but Oakley’s absence did not go unnoticed. Fans immediately questioned why the former Knicks forward was not included. One wrote: “We want Charles Oakley.” Another asked: “They still not letting Charles Oakley in the building?” A third posted: “Where is Charles Oakley?” Oakley has not returned to Madison Square Garden since his ejection during a Knicks game against the Los Angeles Clippers in February 2017. An alleged verbal confrontation with owner James Dolan escalated into a physical scuffle with arena security. The incident culminated a long-running feud between the pair, with Oakley having repeatedly criticised Dolan’s running of the franchise. Although the former Knicks star is not currently under an active ban from the arena, he has not returned since that night. His absence was particularly frustrating for some Knicks supporters, with one tweeting: “Problem here is there’s no Charles Oakley or Patrick Ewing – two of the biggest names in Knicks history.” Another added: “If that DISGRACE Dolan won’t let this man’s name be said, we’re damn well gonna recognize it here… CHARLES OAKLEY! WE appreciate you.” The Knicks did eventually give their fans something to celebrate, as Mikal Bridges hit a buzzer-beating three-pointer to secure a dramatic 97-96 win over Portland. However, Oakley’s absence remained a talking point on a night dedicated to the franchise’s history. item.title: DeVonta Smith is Not Ready to Surrender Amid Eagles’ Brutal 2026 Season
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles are technically still in the race for a spot in the NFL playoffs, but it’s fair to dismiss their chances of playing beyond the regular season. At 2-7 through 10 weeks , Philadelphia is at the bottom of the NFC East Division standings, where the 5-3-1 New York Giants are leading the rest of the group. Still, there is hope for Philadelphia, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith, and that’s all he needs to keep believing in his team. “At the end of the day, you know, it’s not over, especially in this division,” the former Alabama Crimson Tide star wide receiver said, via Ed Kracz of Sports Illustrated . “I feel like there’s still a chance in our division right now. But you can only take it one week at a time, so focusing on this week. Getting the win would be the biggest thing right now; just get back on track.” Eagles’ Smith on Track to Play in Week 11 Nov 28, 2025; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Injuries have played a major part in Philadelphia’s struggles. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is done for the rest of the season with blood clots in his lungs. As for Smith, he’s missed five games already because of a nagging hamstring issue. He missed Weeks 4 and 5 before returning to action in Week 6. However, he sat out the next three games. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team.
